SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SOIL ITS RESOURCES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Soil its resources helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: SOIL ITS RESOURCES
Soil its resources is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Identify ways of playing with  Learners to fill and empty cans soil for enjoyment with soil for fun  Learner to model different objects

What this means
In this part you learn to identify ways of playing with  Learners to fill and empty cans soil for enjoyment with soil for fun  Learner to model different objects. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify ways of playing with  Learners to fill and empty cans soil for enjoyment with soil for fun  Learner to model different objects.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify ways of playing with  Learners to fill and empty cans soil for enjoyment with soil for fun  Learner to model different objects. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Model different objects using  Learners to draw on the soil and soil at school make different patterns using soil

What this means
In this part you learn to model different objects using  Learners to draw on the soil and soil at school make different patterns using soil. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: model different objects using  Learners to draw on the soil and soil at school make different patterns using soil.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can model different objects using  Learners to draw on the soil and soil at school make different patterns using soil. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Soil its resources is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil its resources” around your school. (skill: identify ways of playing with  Learners to fill and empty cans soil for enjoyment with soil for fun  Learner to model different objects)

Example 2: Say why Soil its resources matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: model different objects using  Learners to draw on the soil and soil at school make different patterns using soil)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Soil its resources to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify ways of playing with  Learners to fill and empty cans soil for enjoyment with soil for fun  Learner to model different objects.
3. Practise this skill: model different objects using  Learners to draw on the soil and soil at school make different patterns using soil.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Soil its resources from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Soil its resources: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Soil its resources?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How could we play its resources (10 lessons) learner should be able to: playing with soil with soil?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Soil its resources means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify ways of playing with  Learners to fill and empty cans soil for enjoyment with soil for fun  Learner to model different objects.
5. Be able to: model different objects using  Learners to draw on the soil and soil at school make different patterns using soil.
